name: Autosomal Dominant Hereditary Axonal Motor and Sensory Neuropathy
aliases: Hereditary Motor and Sensory Neuropathy Type II (HMSN II)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for Hereditary Motor and Sensory Neuropathies

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy with sensory loss predominantly in lower limbs
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with reduced amplitude of motor and sensory responses
Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes associated with axonal neuropathy (e.g., MFN2, NEFL)
Histopathological confirmation showing axonal degeneration without significant demyelination

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autosomal dominant family history, characteristic clinical features, and electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended for confirmation but not mandatory for diagnosis.

searchTerms: weakness and muscle loss in hands and feet
loss of strength in fingers and toes
loss of vibration and position sense

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes

searchTerms: tingling and numbness in hands or feet
pins and needles in distal limbs
muscle cramps in hands and feet
mild pain in hands or feet
reduced ability to feel temperature changes

laboratory: Exclusion of acquired neuropathies (e.g., diabetes, vitamin deficiencies)
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
Nerve ultrasound may show reduced nerve cross-sectional area
genetic: Pathogenic variants in MFN2, NEFL, or other axonal neuropathy-associated genes
other: Nerve conduction studies demonstrating reduced amplitude of motor and sensory responses with relatively preserved conduction velocities
Nerve biopsy showing axonal degeneration without demyelination

distinguishingFeatures: Demyelinating neuropathy with slowed nerve conduction velocities
Onset often in first two decades
Genetic mutations in PMP22, MPZ genes
Recurrent focal neuropathies triggered by minor trauma or compression
Usually autosomal dominant with PMP22 deletion

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
Signs of systemic disease or inflammation
references: Harding AE. Classification of the hereditary motor and sensory neuropathies. Lancet. 1981.
Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009.
